r: Your deck hides its best news. The 40% month-over-month revenue growth doesn't appear until slide nine, after three slides of generic market-sizing material. Investors reviewing a seed pitch decide within the first 3 minutes, and DocSend's averages show they often spend under 4 minutes on the whole deck. So the one number your fundraising case depends on shows up after they have stopped paying attention. Your opening slide is a mission statement, but the data should go up front. Make slide two lead with growth, then the customer acquisition cost payback period of 5 months, then the problem. As it stands, readers have to wait for the payoff, and they will either skip ahead to the end or quit. Investors may also assume you hid the numbers on purpose. Cut the market-size introduction to one line and let your traction speak for itself.
